Week 43 / Shuffling picture cards / K–1 Mix the three picture cards in a cup. Each card has the same chance. Draw the first with- out looking and keep it out. Draw the second from the two left. Put the last card at the end. Return all cards for a new row. C A B Example: choose triangle, then square; circle is left. Problem 2: For each crossed-out first card, find every row still possible. Could two different first-two draws make the same row? Bellingham Math Circle / Week 43 / W43-k-1-v2 2

At each draw, all tickets in the cup have equal chances. Reset both sets for every new row. A slot may swap with it- self. 1 2 3 swap with slot 1 2 3 swap with slot 2 A B C 1 with 3 C B A 2 with 2 C B A Problem 3: Start with A B C and choose tickets to make every row. Can any row be made by two different ticket stories? 1 2 3 Bellingham Math Circle / Week 43 / W43-k-1-v2 3

grades-2-3.text: Week 43 / Shuffling picture cards / Grades 2–3 Mix the three picture cards in a cup. Each card has the same chance. Draw the first with- out looking and keep it out. Draw the second from the two left. Put the last card at the end. Return all cards for a new row. C A B Example: choose triangle, then square; circle is left. Problem 1: Find every possible final row. Could the chooser give any row more chance than another? Use the possible choices to decide. Bellingham Math Circle / Week 43 / W43-grades-2-3-v2 1

Week 43 / Shuffling picture cards / Grades 2–3 Start A B C. Mix tickets 1, 2, 3 in the cup; draw and swap its slot with slot 1. Empty the cup, then mix tickets 2, 3; draw and swap its slot with slot 2. At each draw, all tickets in the cup have equal chances. Reset both sets for every new row. A slot may swap with it- self. 1 2 3 swap with slot 1 2 3 swap with slot 2 A B C 1 with 3 C B A 2 with 2 C B A Problem 2: Start with A B C. Match each two-ticket story to the final row it makes. Does this give each row the same chance? 1 2 2 2 3 2 1 3 2 3 3 3 Bellingham Math Circle / Week 43 / W43-grades-2-3-v2 2

Week 43 / Shuffling picture cards / Grades 2–3 Problem 3: Start with B A C and use the same two-swap rule. Can you still make every row? Find the ticket story for each target. A B C A C B B A C B C A C A B C B A Problem 4: A friend says six random shuffles must show all six rows once. Can you make a possible six-shuffle story that settles this? Bellingham Math Circle / Week 43 / W43-grades-2-3-v2 3

Find several different three-ticket stories that give the same final row. Problem 6: There are 27 equally likely three-ticket stories. Could this rule give all six rows the same chance? Bellingham Math Circle / Week 43 / W43-grades-2-3-v2 4

grades-4-5.text: Week 43 / Shuffling picture cards / Grades 4–5 Mix the three picture cards in a cup. Each card has the same chance. Draw the first with- out looking and keep it out. Draw the second from the two left. Put the last card at the end. Return all cards for a new row. C A B Example: choose triangle, then square; circle is left. Problem 1: Does this chooser give every order of A, B, C the same chance? Settle the question using every possible choice story. Bellingham Math Circle / Week 43 / W43-grades-4-5-v2 1

Week 43 / Shuffling picture cards / Grades 4–5 Start A B C. Mix tickets 1, 2, 3 in the cup; draw and swap its slot with slot 1. Empty the cup, then mix tickets 2, 3; draw and swap its slot with slot 2. At each draw, all tickets in the cup have equal chances. Reset both sets for every new row. A slot may swap with it- self. 1 2 3 swap with slot 1 2 3 swap with slot 2 A B C 1 with 3 C B A 2 with 2 C B A Problem 2: Does this two-swap rule give every order the same chance? Find all its choice stories and their final orders. Problem 3: Start with C B A instead. Explain whether the chance of each final order changes, without listing every story again. C B A Bellingham Math Circle / Week 43 / W43-grades-4-5-v2 2

Week 43 / Shuffling picture cards / Grades 4–5 A new rule starts with A B C. Draw from 1, 2, 3 at each step: swap slot 1 with its choice, then slot 2 with its choice, then slot 3 with its choice. Replace and mix after each choice. Problem 4: Can this rule give all six orders the same chance? Find an exact rea- son; a short run of random shuffles cannot settle the question. Problem 5: Another rule forbids swapping a slot with itself. Swap slot 1 with slot 2 or 3, then swap slots 2 and 3. Find every possible final order. Is this a fair shuffle of all six orders? A B C Bellingham Math Circle / Week 43 / W43-grades-4-5-v2 3

Explain why it meets both goals. A B C D Problem 7: Design a fair five-card version on paper with exactly one story for each final order. Specify the ticket sets and resets; how many equally likely stories does your rule have? A B C D E Bellingham Math Circle / Week 43 / W43-grades-4-5-v2 4
